chats.answer:
For a 16-inch laptop, I'd prioritize a triple-screen extender with two additional displays that are 16:10, 1920 × 1200 (WUXGA) rather than the more common 1920 × 1080 panels.

The key is finding one that offers all three:

Two 1920 × 1200 IPS screens, preferably 16 inches each.

Compatibility with 16-inch laptops, without putting excessive weight on the laptop hinges.

Independent extended displays, so your laptop and the two external screens can show three different desktops.

A lot of products advertised as “triple-screen laptop extenders” have 1080p panels, even when the listing says they're compatible with 16-inch laptops. That's the main specification to watch out for.

Best options I found

MagHub Dual Lite 16" Portable Screen Extender

Two 16-inch 1920 × 1200 IPS screens, detachable, driver-free on supported laptops. A good balance of price, resolution, and flexibility.

Two 16-inch 1920 × 1200 IPS displays, with a driver-based connection. Worth considering if your laptop cannot natively drive two external screens.

Two 16-inch 1920 × 1200 IPS screens, 2.4 kg, detachable design, integrated metal support stand, and native USB-C/HDMI video connections. 
Detachable Screens

View manufacturer

My recommendation

For a Windows laptop with two supported video outputs, I'd choose the INVZI MagHub Dual Lite 16". It meets your exact resolution requirement, avoids display-driver installation, and has detachable screens.

One important distinction: the FOPO S788 also matches 1920 × 1200, but it adds three external screens, creating a four-screen setup with your laptop, rather than a three-screen setup. 
FOPO

What is your exact 16-inch laptop model? For example, MacBook Pro 16 M3 Pro, Lenovo ThinkPad P16, or Dell XPS 16. That will determine which extender can run both displays independently without compatibility problems.
